'''Tomaž Prosen''' (born 1970) is a Slovenian [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] and [[mathematical physicist]]. His research has spanned [[Non-equilibrium statistical mechanics|non-equilibrium dynamics]], [[statistical mechanics]], [[Transport phenomena|quantum transport]], and [[chaos theory]].

== Early career ==

Prosen earned his Diploma in Physics in 1991, and a [[Doctorate of Science]] in 1995, both from the [[University of Ljubljana]]. He finished both at a significantly younger age than usual. [[Institute for Scientific Information|ISI]] named him a 'Citation Superstar' as one of the most cited young scientists in Slovenia in 2000.<ref name="Prosen CV">{{Cite web|last=Prosen|first=Tomaz|date=2020-10-07|title=T. Prosen CV (2020)|url=https://chaos.fmf.uni-lj.si/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/ProsenCV2020.pdf|access-date=2020-10-07|website=Tomaz Prosen CV}}</ref> He was made a Full Professor at the University of Ljubljana by outstanding early election in 2008.<ref name="Prosen CV" />

== Research ==

Tomaž Prosen is primarily known for providing the first exact solutions for models of [[Open quantum system|open]] quantum many-body systems and for the discovery of novel kinds of quantum [[conservation laws]] that settled long-standing questions about the nature of [[Transport phenomena|transport]] in fundamental models of low-dimensional quantum materials, such as the [[Heisenberg model (quantum)|Heisenberg spin chains]] and the one-dimensional [[Hubbard model]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Prosen|first=Tomaž|date=2011-05-27|title=Open XXZ Spin Chain: Nonequilibrium Steady State and a Strict Bound on Ballistic Transport|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.217206|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=106|issue=21|article-number=217206|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.217206|pmid=21699339|arxiv=1103.1350|bibcode=2011PhRvL.106u7206P|s2cid=36194016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Prosen|first1=Tomaž|last2=Ilievski|first2=Enej|date=2013-08-02|title=Families of Quasilocal Conservation Laws and Quantum Spin Transport|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.057203|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=111|issue=5|article-number=057203|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.057203|pmid=23952440|arxiv=1306.4498|bibcode=2013PhRvL.111e7203P|s2cid=23359583}}</ref> The latter work also provided a full description of [[canonical ensemble]]s of [[quantum integrable system]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ilievski|first1=E.|last2=De Nardis|first2=J.|last3=Wouters|first3=B.|last4=Caux|first4=J.-S.|last5=Essler|first5=F. H. L.|last6=Prosen|first6=T.|date=2015-10-07|title=Complete Generalized Gibbs Ensembles in an Interacting Theory|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.157201|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=115|issue=15|article-number=157201|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.157201|pmid=26550747|arxiv=1507.02993|bibcode=2015PhRvL.115o7201I|s2cid=500997}}</ref> paving the way for extensions of [[thermodynamics]] to integrable systems. He is also known for pioneering a novel approach for establishing [[quantum chaos]] in [[spin-1/2]] systems, for which previously known [[Semiclassical physics|semi-classical]] methods fail.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Kos|first1=Pavel|last2=Ljubotina|first2=Marko|last3=Prosen|first3=Tomaž|date=2018-06-08|title=Many-Body Quantum Chaos: Analytic Connection to Random Matrix Theory|journal=Physical Review X|volume=8|issue=2|article-number=021062|doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.8.021062|arxiv=1712.02665|bibcode=2018PhRvX...8b1062K|doi-access=free}}</ref> This approach challenged conventional beliefs in theoretical physics by providing an exact solution to the dynamics of a chaotic model.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bertini|first1=Bruno|last2=Kos|first2=Pavel|last3=Prosen|first3=Tomaž|date=2018-12-27|title=Exact Spectral Form Factor in a Minimal Model of Many-Body Quantum Chaos|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.264101|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=121|issue=26|article-number=264101|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.264101|pmid=30636114|arxiv=1805.00931|bibcode=2018PhRvL.121z4101B|s2cid=51696196}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Journal Club for Condensed Matter Physics » Blog Archive » A breakthrough in many body quantum chaos| date=30 June 2018 |url=https://www.condmatjclub.org/?p=3406|access-date=2020-10-07|doi=10.36471/jccm_june_2018_02| s2cid=240432938 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Memberships ==
He is a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members |url=https://members.euro-acad.eu/#memberList |access-date=2024-11-15 |website=members.euro-acad.eu}}</ref> and the [[Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members |url=https://www.sazu.si/en/members/3 |access-date=2024-11-20 |website=www.sazu.si |language=en}}</ref>
